description: Kampala Uganda Temple (KUT) PROJECT OVERLAY for the STING LOD verification matrix. Merged by id/category over the corporate baseline (StingTools/Data/STING_LOD_MATRIX.json) — project milestones/categoryRules win. Deploy to <project>/_BIM_COORD/lod_matrix.json. The six milestones below are the unified A1/A2 reconciliation from proposal Section 3.5 (A1 LOD 300 governs over A2's LOD 200 at Deliverable B; Deliverable C stated at LOD 350 to make coordinated interfaces contractual). LOD LADDER DECISION: Deliverable D (record / as-built model) is verified at LOD 500, NOT the LOD 400 stated in the client's A1 Design Scope of Services. LOD 400 is fabrication/installation maturity and is retained here as the 'construction' milestone covering Work Program item 3.1 (Supervise the Building Construction Contract); LOD 500 is field-verified as-built, which is what a record/handover model is. The A1 figure is read as a drafting error in the client document and this matrix follows the standard LOD ladder. The corporate baseline already matches these — they are restated here as the project's confirmed, client-facing record. Checks are a parameter/naming/geometry-presence maturity proxy, NOT a geometric survey. Add temple-specific category rules below as the design team confirms them. RUNG 500 DIFFERS BY CATEGORY, DELIBERATELY. LOD 500 is field-verified as-built. On SERIALISED, SERVICEABLE PLANT — Mechanical Equipment, Electrical Equipment, Plumbing Fixtures, Lighting Fixtures, Air Terminals, Sprinklers, Fire Alarm Devices, Specialty Equipment — it inherits 400 and adds +ASS_SERIAL_NR_TXT and +ASS_INSTALLATION_DATE_TXT, because that is the O&M/commissioning record the Owner actually receives and what Fohlio publishes. On BUILDING FABRIC AND DISTRIBUTION — Walls, Floors, Doors, Windows, Roofs, Ceilings, Stairs, Railings, Ramps, Curtain Panels, Curtain Wall Mullions, Ducts, Pipes, Duct/Pipe Fittings, Conduits, Cable Trays, Structural Framing/Columns/Foundations, Casework, Furniture, Furniture Systems, Electrical Fixtures, Rooms, and the "*" fallback — rung 500 is a bare inherit of 400 and adds NO required parameters. An installation date on every wall, duct run and pipe segment is not something a general contractor's as-built delivers; demanding it would make the first deliverable-d run report near-total failure on fabric and train the team to ignore the report. The rung still means something on fabric — it carries 400's manufacturer/model requirements — it just stops demanding data nobody produces. Doors and Windows are deliberately in the FABRIC group: they carry manufacturer and model at 400 and are schedule-tracked, but they are not serialised plant. SCOPE: project-wide LOD_Verify collects every taggable model category (LodScope.Collect), so the "*" rule is genuinely reachable, and the run DISCLOSES the categories it did not scan in the TaskDialog, the CSV header and the JSON gate report.
_categoryRulesNote: DELIBERATELY EMPTY. This overlay used to restate the corporate Lighting Fixtures and Plumbing Fixtures rules. Because LodVerificationEngine REPLACES a category rule wholesale (LodVerificationEngine.cs), an overlay copy silently discards every future corporate improvement to that category -- and the two copies had already paid that cost: the Lighting Fixtures rule was byte-identical to corporate (pure loss, no gain), and the Plumbing Fixtures rule had quietly dropped +MNT_TYPE_TXT from rung 400, which corporate has carried since Phase 192 B1 -- BEFORE this overlay was written. That is drift, not a decision: this file's own description claims the rules are 'restated' from corporate. Both are removed, so KUT now inherits the corporate rules for these two categories. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE TO EXPECT: Plumbing Fixtures at LOD 400 (the 'construction' milestone) now require MNT_TYPE_TXT again. Re-add a rule here ONLY to state a genuine temple-specific difference, and when you do, say in this note what the difference is and why.
